title: Bounded Hochschild cohomology of von Neumann algebras
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 manuscript, that every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a von Neumann algebra is the coboundary of a bounded cochain; with the Kadison-Sakai theorem this settles the Kadison-Ringrose cohomology problem. The bounded Hochschild complex and the tracial 2-norm; a rigidity theorem for first-letter identities on free Haar families; a random walk on the unitary group whose long products are asymptotically free; a Liouville theorem for its harmonic maps; bounded primitives by averaging, removal of separability and an explicit central homotopy.
prerequisites: von Neumann algebras: the double commutant theorem, operator topologies and preduals, Kaplansky's density theorem, the spectral theorem, projections and types, W*-algebras (course Foundations of von Neumann algebras)
Haar unitaries, freeness and Popa's free independence theorem in tracial ultraproducts (course Generators of II1 factors, lessons 1 and 2)
the central decomposition and the types of the fibres (course Measurable fields and direct integrals)
trace-preserving conditional expectations (course Traces and noncommutative integration, Theorem 9.1)
tracial ultraproducts (course Type III factors, Ultraproducts and the asymptotic centralizer, Theorem 3.2)
products of probability spaces (core course D10 Measure and Integration, Fremlin, Measure Theory, Theorem 254F)

open_obligations: K1 The normal reduction of Johnson, Kadison and Ringrose (Bull. Soc. Math. France 100 (1972), Lemma 5.4 and Theorem 5.6, Numdam): every bounded cocycle of degree k >= 2 on a von Neumann algebra is cohomologous to a separately normal bounded cocycle. Used in lesson 5, Section 4. Intended home: a lesson on normal cohomology placed after lesson 1 of this course.

K2 Vanishing of bounded Hochschild cohomology in degrees k >= 2 for von Neumann algebras without a type II1 central summand (Kadison-Ringrose, Acta Math. 126 (1971), Theorem 4.4, for type I; Christensen-Effros-Sinclair, Invent. Math. 90 (1987), for the properly infinite case; combined statement in Christensen-Pop-Sinclair-Smith, Ann. of Math. 158 (2003), equation (1.1), arXiv:math/0107078). Used in lesson 5, Section 4. Intended home: lessons on cohomology of type I algebras and on completely bounded multilinear maps.
Not used: the Kadison-Sakai theorem that derivations of von Neumann algebras are inner (degree one), quoted in lesson 1 as context.
